Bai 2022 (immunological / mediator-side review of hypoxia-TAM crosstalk) is complementary to Bhandari 2019 (genome-side pancancer molecular landmarks of tumor hypoxia). Both anchor the hypoxia-cancer axis but on different layers — Bhandari maps the somatic-genome landscape (mutations, CNAs, miR-210, miR-133a-3p, telomere length, nimbosus); Bai synthesizes the immune-mediator dialogue between tumor and TAMs in the same hypoxic regions

Bai 2022 (extrinsic hypoxia-driven tumor → TAM crosstalk review) is complementary to Calafell 2024 (intrinsic NF-κB+TET2-driven hypoxic macrophage reprogramming). Both converge on hypoxic-macrophage phenotype but from opposite directions — Bai describes the external mediators (exosomes, cytokines, oncometabolites) that hypoxic tumors deliver; Calafell describes the cell-intrinsic transcriptional / methylation reprogramming that hypoxic macrophages execute

Bai 2022 (mechanistic review of hypoxia-TAM crosstalk using M1/M2 framing) is complementary to Mulder 2021 (MoMac-VERSE single-cell atlas of pan-tissue mononuclear phagocytes). Bai's M1/M2 dichotomy can be projected onto Mulder's cluster-level taxonomy to identify which cluster (e.g. IL4I1 TAM) is the canonical hypoxic-niche-recruited subset

Bai 2022 (mediator-driven hypoxic-niche TAM mechanisms) is complementary to Casanova-Acebes 2021 (TRM-pioneered NSCLC tumor-immune niche). The recruitment-and-retention model in Bai (Sema3A-NRP1-PlexinA stop signal) explains how monocyte-derived TAMs accumulate in the hypoxic core; Casanova-Acebes shows that the TRM lineage that pre-exists in the niche is the EMT-inducing subset — together they offer a fuller account of who occupies the hypoxic-niche TAM compartment
